pairs: Rectorem te posuerunt?
Have they appointed you as a leader?
noli extolli:
Do not be willing to be extolled.
esto in illis quasi unus ex ipsis.
Be among them as one of them.
Curam illorum habe, et sic conside,
Have concern for them, and in this way sit down with them,
et omni cura tua explicita recumbe:
and when you have explained all your concerns, sit back.
ut læteris propter illos,
Then you may rejoice because of them,
et ornamentum gratiæ accipias coronam,
and you may receive a crown as an adornment of grace,
et dignationem consequaris corrogationis.
and so obtain the dignity of the assembly.
Loquere major natu:
Speak, you who are greater by birth.
decet enim te
For it is fitting for you
primum verbum diligenti scientia,
to speak the first word with careful knowledge.
et non impedias musicam.
But you should not hinder the music.
Ubi auditus non est,
Where no one is listening,
non effundas sermonem,
you should not pour out words.
et importune noli extolli in sapientia tua.
And do not choose to be extolled improperly for your wisdom.
Gemmula carbunculi in ornamento auri,
A gemstone of garnet is set amid an ornament of gold,
et comparatio musicorum in convivio vini.
and a concert of music is set amid a banquet of wine.
Sicut in fabricatione auri signum est smaragdi,
Just as a signet of emerald is set amid a work of gold,
sic numerus musicorum in jucundo et moderato vino.
so is a melody of music set amid delightful and moderate wine.
Audi tacens,
Listen silently,
et pro reverentia accedet tibi bona gratia.
and for your reverence, good graces will be added to you.
Adolescens,
Young man,
loquere in tua causa vix.
speak in your own case only reluctantly.
Si bis interrogatus fueris,
If you have been asked twice,
habeat caput responsum tuum.
let your response be concise.
In multis esto quasi inscius,
In many matters,
et audi tacens simul
be as if you lack knowledge,
et quærens.
and listen silently as well as intently.
In medio magnatorum non præsumas:
In the midst of great men, you should not be presumptuous.
et ubi sunt senes non multum loquaris.
And where the elders are present, you should not speak much.
Ante grandinem præibit coruscatio:
Lightning goes before a hailstorm,
et ante verecundiam præibit gratia,
and grace goes before modesty. And so,
et pro reverentia accedet tibi bona gratia.
for your reverence, good graces will be added to you.
Et hora surgendi non te trices:
And at the hour for rising, you should not be lax.
præcurre autem prior in domum tuam,
Later, be the first to run ahead to your house,
et illic avocare, et illic lude,
and there withdraw, and there take your pastime.
et age conceptiones tuas,
And act according to your intentions,
et non in delictis et verbo superbo:
but not in sin and not in arrogant speech.
et super his omnibus benedicito Dominum,
And for all these things, bless the Lord,
qui fecit,
who made you,
et inebriantem te ab omnibus bonis suis.
and who fills you to overflowing with all his good things.
Qui timet Dominum excipiet doctrinam ejus:
Whoever fears the Lord will accept his doctrine.
et qui vigilaverint ad illum invenient benedictionem.
And whoever watches for him diligently will find a blessing.
Qui quærit legem replebitur ab ea,
Whoever seeks the law will be filled from the law.
et qui insidiose agit scandalizabitur in ea.
But whoever acts with treachery will be scandalized by treachery.
Qui timent Dominum invenient judicium justum,
Those who fear the Lord will find just judgment,
et justitias quasi lumen accendent.
and they will kindle justice like a light.
Peccator homo vitabit correptionem,
A sinful man will shun correction,
et secundum voluntatem suam inveniet comparationem.
and he will find a rationalization in accord with his own will.
Vir consilii non disperdet intelligentiam:
A man of counsel will not reject understanding.
alienus et superbus non pertimescet timorem:
A strange and arrogant man will not be disturbed by fear.
etiam postquam fecit cum eo sine consilio,
Even so, after he has acted out of fear and without counsel,
et suis insectationibus arguetur.
he will be rebuked by his own criticism.
Fili,
Son,
sine consilio nihil facias,
you should do nothing without counsel,
et post factum non pœnitebis.
and then you will not regret what you have done.
In via ruinæ non eas,
You should not go into the way of ruin,
et non offendes in lapides:
and you then will not stumble on stones.
nec credas te viæ laboriosæ,
You should not commit yourself to a laborious way;
ne ponas animæ tuæ scandalum.
otherwise, you may set up a scandal against your own soul.
Et a filiis tuis cave,
And be cautious concerning your own sons.
et a domesticis tuis attende.
And be attentive to those of your own household.
In omni opere tuo crede ex fide animæ tuæ,
In all of your works, trust your soul to faith.
hoc est enim conservatio mandatorum.
For this is the keeping of the commandments.
Qui credit Deo attendit mandatis:
Whoever believes God attends to the commandments.
et qui confidit in illo non minorabitur.
And whoever trusts in him will not be diminished.
